model: FCFE at cost of equity (engine route) - electronic broker, consolidated flows on as-if-exchanged IBG LLC units

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Year-1 base growth off the TTM run-rate, anchored to H1-2026 (+22.6% YoY) less the disclosed NII drag of ~1.2% of revenue per 25bp Fed cut and a normalising account-growth rate; roughly sell-side FY2027 net-revenue growth. Historical CAGRs are rate-cycle inflated (Fed funds 0.1% -> 4.3% between FY2021 and FY2024 lifted NII from 1,148 to 3,148) and are NOT projected.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (20.8% 3yr) is >30% below EPS CAGR (33.3%) and attributable-NI CAGR (37.3%): the gap is (a) NII leverage to the 2022-24 rate cycle, (b) 78% earnings retention building excess capital, and (c) IBG Inc.'s rising ownership share (18.5% FY2019 -> 26.5%) lifting per-share attributable growth above consolidated growth. None of the three recurs at the historical rate.
historical_growth.notes: Net revenue = us-gaap:RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense (FY2020 2,218; FY2021 2,714; FY2022 3,067; FY2023 4,340; FY2024 5,185; FY2025 6,205). EPS split-adjusted (4:1 Jun-2023): FY2020 0.605, FY2022 0.9375, FY2025 2.22. Equity = total incl. NCI (FY2020 9,003; FY2022 11,615; FY2025 20,472). 'fcf' CAGRs are consolidated net income (FY2020 1,179; FY2022 1,842; FY2025 4,357) -- there is no meaningful FCF series for a broker. Attributable NI: FY2020 195; FY2022 380; FY2025 984.

scenario_narratives.base: Account growth normalises from +34% toward low-teens as the international cohort matures; Fed funds settles ~3% (another ~2-3 cuts, ~-$250M NII against a still-growing margin book); commissions keep tracking DARTs and customer equity. Net revenue +14% in the year to Jun-2027 decelerating to 3.5% by year 10; pretax margin eases from 78% to 72% as NII mix falls.
scenario_narratives.bull: International account growth stays above 25% for three more years, prediction markets and crypto add a third commission leg, the Fed pauses near 3.5% so margin-loan growth more than offsets rate drag, and the 77-78% pretax margin holds for a decade.
scenario_narratives.bear: Fed funds falls to ~2.5% into a risk-asset drawdown that shrinks the margin book and DARTs together; zero-commission competition caps commission yields; a margin-liquidation loss adds to bad debt. Revenue flat for two years, pretax margin back to the pre-2023 66%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: IBKR is valued as a stream of free cash flow to equity at a 10% cost of equity, not as an operating-company owner-FCF DCF: consolidated net revenues (which are already net of interest expense) are taken to pretax income at the automated-broker margin, taxed at the ~21.5% all-in rate the public holder bears on its 26.5% share of the IBG LLC partnership, charged with the regulatory-capital retention that a growing margin-loan book requires (about $1.25 per $1 of revenue growth), and divided by the as-if-exchanged 1,698M IBG LLC units so that per-unit value equals per-Class-A value. Net debt is held at zero because the balance sheet is customer money; the $14.2B of excess regulatory capital (~$8/unit at face) is valued only through the interest it earns inside NII. The market price at ~35-40x attributable earnings is paying for the bull case at a sub-10% discount rate; the house value at 10% and a 3% terminal growth sits well below it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Interest-rate path: ~$81M of annual NII per 25bp of Fed funds (~1.2% of revenue per cut); a return toward 2% would push the base case toward the bear margin path

Retention assumption: if regulatory capital keeps compounding with margin loans (+67% YoY) faster than with revenue, the -125% capture understates the cash the business must keep; if IBKR ever distributes the $14.2B excess, value rises by up to ~$8/unit
Ownership/tax: the all-in tax rate depends on IBG Inc.'s share and on redemption step-ups; a 2pp change moves value ~2.5%
Terminal multiple: Gordon at 10%/3% (14.7x FCFE) binds below the 16x cap; a 9% cost of equity alone adds roughly a fifth to value (see required_return_table)
Governance: Holdings controls ~90% of votes; the low Class A payout (0.4% yield) is a founder choice the model does not assume changes

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 58.95-98.75
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1381197): RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense, InterestIncomeExpenseNet, IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxes..., ProfitLoss, NetIncomeLossAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest, EarningsPerShareDiluted, WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding, ExcessCapital, AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense; Q2-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-06) for the 26.5% ownership table, note 15 regulatory capital, D&A and capex; IBKR_Metrics.csv for equity, cash and consolidated NI history
data_sources.qualitative: IBKR_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): business mix, $81M/25bp NII sensitivity, account/customer-equity/margin-loan growth, bull and bear cases

inputs.base_revenue_basis: TTM net revenues to 2026-06-30 (us-gaap:RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense): FY2025 6,205 - H1-2025 2,907 + H1-2026 3,565. Net of interest expense, so the flow is already post-funding-cost; commissions ~35%, NII ~56% (TTM NII 3,894).
inputs.share_count_basis: As-if-exchanged IBG LLC membership interests: Q2-2026 diluted weighted-average Class A count 450.088M (10-Q) / IBG Inc.'s 26.5% ownership of IBG LLC at 2026-06-30 = 1,698.4M units. Each Holdings unit exchanges 1:1 into a Class A share, so value per unit equals value per Class A share. The annual Holdings redemption (2.50M Class A issued Jul-2026, 3.84M Jul-2025) raises IBG Inc.'s ownership % and the Class A count together and is per-share neutral; total units are held FLAT. SBC is expensed in the flows, so no separate dilution.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Broker balance sheet: no corporate borrowings (10-Q: 'no variable-rate debt outstanding'); the $7.7B cash line and the $247B of assets are customer-funded operating balances (segregated cash, margin loans, securities borrowed), not net cash or net debt. Held at zero per the bank/broker rule; the firm's own equity capital earns interest that is already inside NII.
inputs.fcf_basis: reported_fcf = TTM consolidated pretax income 5,356 taxed at the 21.5% all-in rate IBG Inc. bears on its share, with SBC added back (street basis); last_fcf = the same after the SBC charge = earnings-equivalent FCFE BEFORE the required-capital retention, which the engine applies each forecast year through wc_capture_pct. Reported OCF (15,811 FY2025) is customer-balance noise and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense, TTM to Jun-2026: FY2025 118 - H1-2025 59 + H1-2026 65 = 124 (10-K/10-Q cash-flow add-back 'Employee stock plan compensation'). No separate net-share-settlement tax line disclosed; IBKR settles awards in shares.
inputs.buyback_note: No Class A repurchases (no PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock tag). Distributions are the $0.35/yr Class A dividend (raised to $0.0875/qtr Jun-2026; $75M H1-2026) and $512M H1-2026 of IBG LLC distributions to Holdings for its members' taxes and dividends.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC: the flow is post-interest and no debt is subtracted. USD build: 10-yr UST ~4.2% + 1.15 beta x 5.0% ERP = 9.95%, rounded to 10.0%. Single rate across scenarios (risk charged once, through the scenario weights).
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases stay inside noninterest expense (occupancy line, ~$54M H1-2026); no lease liability in net debt and no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: The 73.5% non-controlling interest (IBG Holdings / Peterffy) is NOT deducted: flows are consolidated and the divisor is the as-if-exchanged unit count, so Holdings' share is charged through the denominator exactly once. Cross-check FY2025: attributable NI 984 / 443.9M Class A = $2.22 diluted EPS; consolidated 4,771 pretax x (1-0.215) / (443.9/0.262 = 1,694M units) = $2.21.
inputs.tax_basis: Consolidated GAAP tax (414 FY2025, 8.7%) understates the public holder's burden because IBG LLC is a partnership and Holdings' members pay their own tax. All-in rate on IBG Inc.'s share = 1 - 984 / (26.2% x 4,771) = 21.3% FY2025; 20.6% on TTM at 26.5%. Base 21.5%, bull 21.0%, bear 22.5%. Cash taxes run lower (316 paid vs 414 expense FY2025) from redemption basis step-ups; not credited.
inputs.retention_basis: Regulated broker-dealers must retain capital as margin loans and customer balances grow. Required capital = total equity 22,250 - excess regulatory capital 14,193 (10-Q note 15) = 8,057 at 2026-06-30 = 1.17x TTM net revenue, up from 4,252 at Mar-2024. Modelled as wc_capture_pct = -125 (each $1 of revenue growth retains $1.25 of earnings). The $14.2B excess (~$8.4/unit at face) is NOT added to the bridge: its interest is inside NII and the flows, and management holds it as a permanent feature, so it is valued only through the income it earns.
inputs.notes: Model: FCFE at cost of equity through the Drivers engine (routing table has no broker row; nearest rows are bank/insurer, and the house precedent for financials -- NAB.AX, HBAN, GL, IAG.AX -- is FCFE-at-CoE with net_debt = 0). An owner-FCF operating DCF is meaningless here: OCF swings with customer balances (FY2025 15,811 vs NI 4,357), there is no cost of revenue, EBITDA or capex line, and 'net cash' is customer money. Engine mapping: ebitda_margin_path = pretax margin + SBC% (1.8) + D&A% (1.0), so EBIT in the engine equals reported pretax income; capex 1.3% vs D&A 1.0% matches the H1-2026 cash-flow statement (purchases 44, D&A 33 per half); cash_tax_rate = all-in public-holder rate; wc_capture = regulatory-capital retention; terminal cap 16x FCFE (Gordon at 10%/3% = 14.7x binds). The CSV Revenue column (2,440 FY2025) is the ASC-606 fee subset and is NOT the base -- see base_revenue_basis. IBKR gives no revenue/EPS guidance; the one forward disclosure is ~$81M annual NII per 25bp of Fed funds, i.e. ~1.2% of revenue per cut, embedded in the growth and margin paths. Price is the 2026-09-28 regular close, not an after-hours print; refresh_price.py replaces it.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: = pretax margin [74, 70, 68, 67, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66] + 2.8: back to the FY2021-22 65-66% margin once NII is no longer the swing line.
bear.narrative: Fed funds falls to ~2.5% (~-$550M NII, 8% of revenue) into a risk-asset drawdown that shrinks the $108B margin book and DARTs together; zero-commission competition caps commission yields; a margin-liquidation loss event adds to bad debt. Net revenue flat over two years then recovers at 3-4%; pretax margin retreats to the pre-2023 66%; terminal growth 2.5%.

base.ebitda_margin_note: = pretax margin [76, 75, 74, 73.5, 73, 72.5, 72, 72, 72, 72] + SBC 1.8 + D&A 1.0. TTM pretax margin 78.0% (FY2025 76.9%, FY2024 71.3%, FY2022 65.1%): drifts down as Fed cuts compress NII (near-100% incremental margin) faster than automation lowers the cost base.
base.narrative: Account growth normalises from +34% toward low-teens as the international cohort matures; Fed funds settles ~3% (another ~2-3 cuts, ~-$250M NII against a still-growing margin book); commissions keep tracking DARTs and customer equity. Net revenue +14% in the year to Jun-2027 decelerating to 3.5% by year 10; pretax margin eases from 78% to 72% as NII mix falls. Retention of 1.25x revenue growth funds regulatory capital.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: = pretax margin [78, 78, 77.5, 77.5, 77, 77, 77, 77, 77, 77] + 2.8: Q2-2026 77% pretax margin held as automation offsets rate cuts.
bull.narrative: International account growth stays above 25% for three more years, prediction markets (Kalshi/CME/ForecastEx hub) and crypto add a third commission leg, the Fed pauses near 3.5% so margin-loan growth (+67% YoY) more than offsets rate drag, and the 77-78% pretax margin holds for a decade. Net revenue +20% year 1 decelerating to 4% by year 10; terminal growth 3.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 moved to 20/50/30. Bear raised to 20% because the largest profit line (NII, 56% of revenue) is a direct function of a Fed easing cycle already under way and the analysis rates that risk high, and because a $108B margin book growing 67% YoY carries a liquidation-loss tail. Bull trimmed to 30% because holding a 77% pretax margin AND 20% growth through rate cuts requires both the international account engine and the new prediction-market/crypto legs to deliver together. No going-concern or single-regulator dependency, so bear stays at 20% rather than 25-35%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
